cat > /tmp/pr-app-access-body.md << 'EOF'
## Summary

`DirectusRole` created policies with no `app_access` field. Directus defaults that to `false`
(API-only) — so every role this resource creates (Staff, Coach, Guardian) was silently unusable for
actually signing into the Directus Data Studio, even though authentication itself succeeds. Surfaced
tonight: first real login attempt (Google OIDC as `ungood`, Staff role) got "No App Access" right
after a successful sign-in.

## Change

Made `appAccess` a required field on `DirectusRoleArgs`/`DirectusRoleInputs` (no default — this bug
was exactly a silent-default problem, didn't want to trade one default for another) and set it on
the policy in both `create` and `update`. `people-hub.ts`: `true` for Staff/Coach (real users signing
into the app), `false` for Guardian (no login path yet — will be a future end-user-facing portal, not
the Directus app itself, per its own "No login yet" comment).

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` passes.
- [x] Verified against a real local Directus 12.3.1 instance: created a policy with no `app_access`
      field (mirroring the bug) and confirmed `/auth/login` succeeds fine (200, valid JWT) but the
      token carries `"app_access":false` — confirms the failure is a Data Studio (app-level) gate on
      an otherwise-successful login, not an auth failure, matching what was actually observed.

Related to tonight's #99/#101 deploy work but a distinct pre-existing bug (from #97), not something
those PRs touch.
EOF
gh pr create --fill --base main --body-file /tmp/pr-app-access-body.md

# The substrate VM's whole compose stack: every surface behind the one shared Caddy container,
# routed by hostname. Today that's the cycsail.team portal (gated by oauth2-proxy) and the people
# hub (Directus, its own native Google OIDC login — no oauth2-proxy needed for that surface). Secret
# values come from an env file written at boot from Secret Manager (see cloud-init in
# infrastructure/src/substrate-bootstrap.ts) — nothing sensitive lives in git.
services:
  caddy:
    image: ${CADDY_IMAGE}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SITE_DOMAIN: ${SITE_DOMAIN}
      CRM_DOMAIN: ${CRM_DOMAIN}
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    depends_on:
      - oauth2-proxy
      - directus

  oauth2-proxy:
    image: quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.6.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - --http-address=0.0.0.0:4180
      - --reverse-proxy=true
      # Auth-only in front of Caddy: oauth2-proxy makes the allow/deny decision; Caddy serves.
      - --upstream=static://202
      - --provider=google
      - --redirect-url=https://${SITE_DOMAIN}/oauth2/callback
      - --cookie-domain=${SITE_DOMAIN}
      - --whitelist-domain=${SITE_DOMAIN}
      # Accept any Google account (personal Gmail included); the group check below is the real gate.
      - --email-domain=*
      # Authorization = membership in the all@ group (which nests staff@, volunteers@, …).
      - --google-group=${OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_GROUP}
      - --google-admin-email=${OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_ADMIN_EMAIL}
      # Use the VM's own service account (Application Default Credentials via the metadata server)
      # for the Directory API group lookup — no long-lived key file. The substrate SA must have
      # domain-wide delegation for admin.directory.group.readonly (see ../README.md).
      - --google-use-application-default-credentials=true
      - --set-xauthrequest=true
    environment:
      # Shared platform-wide Google OAuth client (substrate.ts) — SSO between this and Directus.
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET: ${OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET}

  # The people hub. Talks to its own database on the shared Cloud SQL instance over private IP
  # (no Cloud SQL Auth Proxy needed — the VM and Cloud SQL are on the same VPC).
  #
  # Directus 12+ (MSCL-licensed) gates custom/relational permission rules (the $CURRENT_USER-scoped
  # filters the Guardian policy depends on — see docs/people-hub-schema.md) behind a license; CYC
  # has one via Directus's Open Innovation Grant (nonprofit, well under the $5M revenue / 50
  # employee thresholds — see docs/manual-setup.md §6). LICENSE_KEY below is required for the
  # Guardian role to actually work, not just for this version number.
  directus:
    image: directus/directus:12.3.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      KEY: ${DIRECTUS_KEY}
      SECRET: ${DIRECTUS_SECRET}
      LICENSE_KEY: ${DIRECTUS_LICENSE_KEY}
      DB_CLIENT: pg
      DB_HOST: ${DIRECTUS_DB_HOST}
      DB_PORT: "5432"
      DB_DATABASE: directus
      DB_USER: directus
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DIRECTUS_DB_PASSWORD}
      ADMIN_EMAIL: ${DIRECTUS_ADMIN_EMAIL}
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${DIRECTUS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      PUBLIC_URL: https://${CRM_DOMAIN}
      # Native Google OIDC, same shared client as oauth2-proxy above — see
      # docs/manual-setup.md for the one-time OAuth client setup. No oauth2-proxy in front of this
      # surface; Directus enforces its own login + roles.
      AUTH_PROVIDERS: google
      AUTH_GOOGLE_DRIVER: openid
      AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      AUTH_GOOGLE_ISSUER_URL: https://accounts.google.com
      AUTH_GOOGLE_IDENTIFIER_KEY: email
      AUTH_GOOGLE_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION: "false"

volumes:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

    environment:

content.thinking:
Since cloud-init won't rerun on the VM, I realize just updating the substrate-image isn't enough — the running caddy/directus containers won't pick up the new image or env vars automatically, so I'll need to manually recreate the containers on the VM.

So the box is actually running the original config from first boot, with the old CRM_DOMAIN and none of tonight's DIRECTUS_DOMAIN or docker-compose updates baked in — the license key fix was the only manual patch applied. That means docker-compose.yml itself is also stuck on the old version since it's only written via cloud-init on first boot, so I'll need to manually push the updated compose file too, or just force a full VM recreation so cloud-init reruns everything cleanly.

Given how many manual patches we've already layered on tonight, the safest move now is to just destroy and let Pulumi recreate the VM from scratch — that way cloud-init applies the port-conflict fix, new domain, and updated compose file consistently in one fresh boot, and since Postgres is already bootstrapped with an admin, this should come up clean.

Since metadata changes apply in-place and won't trigger recreation automatically, I'd need to force it with `pulumi up --replace <urn>` or a targeted replace. Recreating should be safe since the VM is stateless — Directus's real data lives in Cloud SQL, not on the VM, and Caddy's TLS certs persist in a named Docker volume rather than the boot disk.

But that volume lives on the VM's local disk too, so recreation will wipe the cached certs, forcing Caddy to re-issue via ACME for both domains — a harmless one-time reissue given the low traffic. Since we just fixed the actual root-cause bug behind the port conflict, letting the now-corrected cloud-init rebuild the VM cleanly seems like the right move instead of continuing with fragile manual patches.

Recreating it is also the only real way to confirm the fixes hold on a genuine fresh boot, since everything so far has been spliced in manually over SSH. I'll grab the substrate compute instance's URN and use `pulumi up --target-replace` on it, folding in the rest of tonight's diff.

Now I need to figure out a proper strategy for the static-IP conflict, starting with considering setting deleteBeforeReplace on the compute resource.

I'm weighing whether to apply this as a one-off CLI decision versus baking it into the code permanently — since the VM is stateless behind a stable Address resource and downtime is already acceptable during legitimate replaces, making deleteBeforeReplace a persistent default policy in compute.ts seems reasonable rather than a one-time flag.

## Summary

Forcing a replace on the substrate VM tonight (to pick up cloud-init changes without waiting for a
future natural replacement) failed: `Invalid resource usage: 'External IP address: ... is already
in-use.'`. The instance's only external IP is the fixed `substrate` Address, intentionally reused
across replacements so DNS survives them — but that means Pulumi's default create-before-delete
strategy can never work for this resource; a static external IP can't be attached to two instances
at once.

## Change

`deleteBeforeReplace: true` on the instance. Trades a moment of downtime during any future replace
for one that actually succeeds — acceptable for what's already a stateless container host (state
lives in Cloud SQL / Secret Manager, not on the VM).

- Can't easily test a real replace in CI; verified by hand tonight (this is literally the fix for a
  replace that failed live).

Closes nothing (no issue filed — surfaced live tonight while working #99/#101).
EOF
)"

input.command:
cat > /tmp/pr-100-consolidated.md << 'EOF'
## Summary

Everything from tonight's work getting the people-hub/Directus deploy live for the first time,
consolidated into one PR (was split across #100-#106; squashed into this one on request).

- **Admin bootstrap trigger fix (#99):** cloud-init now tears down containers from any other
  compose project before bringing its own up — the pre-substrate-rename `portal` project was never
  torn down and held ports 80/443, plausibly interrupting Directus mid-bootstrap before it seeded
  the admin user. Extracted the cloud-init string-templating into a pulumi-free
  `substrate-bootstrap-script.ts` so it's unit testable.
- **Secret ordering:** `getSecretVersionOutput` for the admin bootstrap password now `dependsOn`
  the secret's own `SecretVersion` write — no implicit ordering existed before.
- **Schema version mismatch (#101):** `schema.yaml`'s recorded `directus: 11.17.4` didn't match the
  pinned `12.3.1` image, so `/schema/diff` always 400'd. Bumped to `12.3.1` — verified the schema
  content itself was already compatible.
- **`crm.<domain>` -> `directus.<domain>`:** Directus is the data layer's admin screen, not a
  customer-facing CRM surface. Renamed the subdomain, DNS record, compose env var
  (`CRM_DOMAIN` -> `DIRECTUS_DOMAIN`, including a spot in `docker-compose.yml` missed in the first
  pass), and internal identifiers to match.
- **`app_access` bug:** `DirectusRole` never set `app_access` on the policies it creates, so every
  role defaulted to API-only access — real users could authenticate fine but got "No App Access"
  the moment the Data Studio itself checked the token. Made `appAccess` a required field (no
  default, given this was exactly a silent-default bug) — `true` for Staff/Coach, `false` for
  Guardian (no login path yet).
- **VM replace fixes:** the substrate VM's only external IP is a fixed `Address` reused across
  replacements (so DNS survives them) — that means a normal create-before-delete replace can never
  work. Added `deleteBeforeReplace: true`. Also moved the VM from `us-west1-a` to `us-west1-b` after
  hitting a real `e2-medium` capacity shortage in `-a` mid-replace tonight (a live outage, already
  fixed in production; this just tracks it in git).

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` passes.
- [x] New unit tests for the compose-project cleanup ordering.
- [x] Verified live end-to-end tonight: admin bootstrap succeeds, schema/roles/your-account all
      deploy, `directus.cycsail.team` serves Directus with a working admin login (`app_access`
      fixed), portal still healthy on the same static IP after the VM move.
- [x] Schema-version and `app_access` fixes were each verified by hand against real local Directus
      12.3.1 containers before being applied live (see individual commit messages for exact repro
      steps).

Fixes #99. Fixes #101.
EOF

content.thinking:
The user can log in now but the Data Studio shows no collections, so I need to figure out why. The `people-hub-schema` DirectusSchema resource did succeed earlier and the diff/apply should have created collections like `people` and `registrations`.

But I'm now questioning whether that schema resource actually completed during the latest successful update (update 94, on the new us-west1-b VM) versus getting stuck during earlier failed VM attempts. I only looked at a tail of the output from update 94, so I haven't actually confirmed the schema resource finished updating rather than just showing as "updating" in that partial view.

Given the overall result was "succeeded" though, all resources including the schema one must have completed without error, so it should have applied — yet the user reports no collections exist. I should check directly against Directus's live /collections endpoint, maybe by SSHing into the VM and using the bootstrap admin credentials, to see what schema state actually exists; there's also a chance the schema diff call returned null (already in sync) and skipped the apply step entirely, which would explain the missing collections despite a "successful" run.

But then I recall the VM migration to us-west1-b was a full wipe+recreate of the VM itself, not the Cloud SQL database — so the directus DB and its wiped/reseeded admin user should still be intact across that VM recreation, since Cloud SQL is separate infrastructure untouched by the VM changes.

So Directus's fresh container boot on the new VM would just find matching migrations and existing users and skip seeding — that part's fine. The real question is whether the schema was ever successfully applied before tonight's events, since Pulumi's people-hub-schema resource forced an update this time due to the baseUrl change, calling applySchema again with the current schema.yaml against whatever state already existed in the DB.

Actually, the very first successful `pulumi up` earlier tonight created people-hub-schema fresh via `create()`, which should have applied the schema and created the collections — and since Cloud SQL data isn't wiped by VM recreations, those collections should still be sitting in the directus database untouched by all the later VM churn. So the collections should exist, but the user's live admin UI shows none, which means either they're genuinely missing or something else is going on.

It's possible the schema exists in the database but is being hidden from view — maybe collection metadata has `hidden: true`, or the user's role lacks read permission on the schema introspection tables, so the Data Studio sidebar shows nothing even though the tables are physically present. I'm now wondering whether the STAFF role's CRUD permissions on collections like people, medical_profiles, and contacts actually translate into sidebar visibility, since Directus requires both read permission on the specific collection and that it not be marked hidden for it to appear in navigation.

Rather than keep speculating about UI permission nuances, the faster approach is to directly verify server-side whether these collections actually exist through the API. That means I'd need to SSH into the VM to fetch admin credentials and query locally — but that's the same pattern as pulling secrets for the license-key fix, which is exactly the kind of credential access I should avoid rather than pursue.
